setlist.title: It Must Have Been the Roses

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Eyes of the World** (3 reviews): Band is so eager to jam that Eyes takes about three minutes to get going; Eyes of the World is described as blazing [4][7][12]
- **Jack-A-Roe** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls this the best Jack-A-Roe ever; Jack-A-Roe has a slow, funky groove that gives the song a different feel [7][8]
- **Ship of Fools** (2 reviews): Ship of Fools is played unhurriedly, with carefully chosen notes; Ship of Fools features very passionate vocals and many extra touches [6][12]
- **Stella Blue** (2 reviews): Stella Blue runs about fifteen minutes, with Jerry's guitar tone praised throughout; Stella Blue is slow and dynamic, with inspired phrasing from Jerry on vocals and guitar [5][12]
- **Mexicali Blues** (1 review): Mexicali Blues is singled out as especially bouncy [5]
- **It Must Have Been the Roses** (1 review): It Must Have Been the Roses is called flawless [5]
- **Lazy Lightning** (1 review): Lazy Lightning leads into Supplication, not into High Time [10]
- **High Time** (1 review): High Time gets a patient, well-considered treatment without rushing anywhere [6]

## The recordings

- **gd77-05-18.sbd.murphy.5596.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 173 min; rated 4.78/5 by 27 [1]. Said about its sound: Clear mix with deep bass; Faint ghost music can be heard between many songs, as if something was taped over [13][14]
- **gd1977-05-18.sbd.miller.79012.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 177 min; rated 4.72/5 by 47 [2]. Said about its sound: Radio bleeds through faintly, audible only during tuning between some songs [2]
- **gd77-05-18.sbd.ladner.4618.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 173 min; rated 4.27/5 by 15 [3]. Said about its sound: Not pristine or pop-free, but far better than a recording made from the parking lot [7]

## Around the show

- Reviewer rates the show alongside Cornell and the previous night, above most spring '77 shows [4]
- Another hot Supplication is found on William and Mary, 9/24/76 [10]
- Many other 1977 Estimated>Eyes pairings are as good or better, Oklahoma for one [10]
- This Music Never Stopped is enjoyable but a little behind the 5/7/77 version [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd77-05-18.sbd.murphy.5596.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Listener infers the ghost music means another analog generation, perhaps a reel, in the lineage; Soundboard to DAT to CDRs, then EAC, WAV and SHN; encoded by Patrick Murphy from Alan Topal seed discs [1][14]
- **gd1977-05-18.sbd.miller.79012.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel (7 inch reels @ 7.5ips 1/2trk) -> Dat (44.1k) D [2]. Also: Uploader confirms this copy comes from the vault master reel; A reel flip during The Other One was repaired with a crossfade [2]
- **gd77-05-18.sbd.ladner.4618.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]
